headline: A suspected China-nexus crew rooted firewalls with the PHP2Shell bugs and breached a United States government-affiliated network, while Lumen exposed Silent Train, the rotating relay network Volt Typhoon rides into American critical infrastructure.

emerging_trends.text: Chinese operators keep turning other people's network gear into their launch pads, with Volt Typhoon's Silent Train chaining hijacked home routers and enterprise boxes to mask four zero-day campaigns and Cisco Talos tracing the KeyDrift implant to UAT-11473, which bypassed authentication on SD-WAN Catalyst Controllers through CVE-2026-20127.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Volt Typhoon's Silent Train Masks Zero-Days

emerging_trends.text: The window between a vendor patch and internet-wide probing now runs days, as Defused Cyber watched scanning start for the Oracle E-Business Suite flaw CVE-2026-101767 one week after Oracle shipped the fix and researchers revealed that the PeopleSoft bug ShinyHunters has worked since May 2026 chains three separate weaknesses.

Machines now hunt the bugs on both sides of the fight: Anthropic's unreleased model chained Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows, and Linux flaws into working exploits in the lab, an autonomous system dug four long-hidden flaws out of EPICS Base, and TrendAI found one attacker server running 44 AI agents against Japanese targets.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Models Chain Browser and Kernel Flaws Into Exploits

topics.title: Brotli Exploitation Hits Magento Stores
topics.latest_developments: CISA confirmed active exploitation of CVE-2026-111497, the Brotli flaw researchers call Node2Shell, Broccoli2Shell, and HTTP2Shell, and two honeypot operators logged attempts, one of them firing a broken exploit; Sophos published its own confirmation of exploitation in the wild; and separately attackers breached hundreds of Adobe Commerce and Magento stores through CVE-2026-48356 in a campaign researchers named PolyShell.
topics.summary: CVE-2026-111497 is an unchecked return value rated 9.2 in Google's Brotli compression library that runs an attacker's code in any application decompressing attacker-supplied Brotli data, among them Node.js, .NET, PowerShell, Bun, and the Python brotli packages. Update the bundling runtime and patch Adobe Commerce and Magento, where CVE-2026-48356 allows an unrestricted file upload.

topics.title: ShinyHunters Chained Three PeopleSoft Flaws
topics.latest_developments: The threat intelligence firm Defused Cyber reported that attackers have begun probing the internet for CVE-2026-101767, the unauthenticated SQL injection rated 9.8 in the Oracle Application Object Library of Oracle E-Business Suite that Oracle patched a week ago, and the researchers who reported the PeopleSoft bug ShinyHunters has exploited since May 2026 said this week it is three flaws chained together, rooted in a server-side request forgery that reaches an internal management interface because PeopleSoft trusts its own loopback address, all of which Oracle patched under the single identifier CVE-2026-35273 in June 2026.
topics.summary: PeopleSoft operators who skipped the June 2026 Oracle patch remain exposed to the full chain, and E-Business Suite administrators should apply the October 2026 Critical Patch Update now that scanning has started. Both products sit on human resources and financial data.

sources.title: ShinyHunters-Exploited Oracle PeopleSoft Zero-Day Turns Out to Be Three Chained Flaws

topics.title: So-net and the Supplier Breach Chain
topics.latest_developments: Sony Network Communications disclosed that attackers reached the So-net member database and took personal information on more than 2.58 million current and former customers of the Japanese internet provider plus the email passwords of 54,401 users; Kroll's Data Breach Outlook 2026 found nearly seven in ten people in the breaches it handled lost data an outside supplier held; His Majesty's Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire and Rescue Services reported British police data leaking several times this decade through third-party information technology suppliers; and a card skimming crew hijacked the shared analytics script of the e-commerce platform Convertr to lift shoppers' payment details at checkout.
topics.summary: So-net customers should change email passwords immediately and watch for credential reuse elsewhere. The wider pattern puts the work on vendor inventories: know which suppliers hold your customer records and which third-party scripts load on your checkout pages.

topics.title: AI Models Chain Browser and Kernel Flaws Into Exploits
topics.latest_developments: Anthropic reported that an unreleased model found flaws in Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows, and Linux and chained them into working proof-of-concept exploits in the lab, with every vendor notified and every bug already patched; an autonomous system uncovered four long-hidden flaws in EPICS Base, the control software behind particle accelerators and fusion labs, the worst rated 9.8; and TrendAI dissected three exposed attacker server environments, one of which ran 44 AI agents against organizations in Japan.
topics.summary: EPICS Base releases 7.0.10 and earlier carry CVE-2026-114595 through CVE-2026-114598, which crash processes, corrupt memory, leak data, and may run code; research facilities should upgrade. Defenders should assume attackers operate the same flaw-finding and attack-automation tooling.

topics.title: Ransomware Affiliate Draws 70 Months
topics.latest_developments: Artem Stryzhak, a 36-year-old Ukrainian national who pleaded guilty in December 2025 to running Nefilim and Hive ransomware attacks on hospitals, government bodies, law firms, and high-revenue companies between 2018 and 2021, drew 70 months in prison, and the Justice Department posted an $11 million reward for information on his co-conspirator; the department also seized virtualine.net, the domain of the bulletproof hosting provider Virtualine, which it says carried sexually explicit images of minors and nonconsensual intimate imagery and laundered bitcoin for its customers; and prosecutors indicted a Malaysian national after a sting in Madagascar broke up a scam compound operation, part of an action against five foreign nationals.
topics.summary: The three moves land within a day of each other and hit different layers of the criminal economy: an intrusion affiliate, the hosting that shelters criminal services, and the scam-center industry now spreading beyond Southeast Asia. Victims of Nefilim and Hive can expect restitution proceedings to follow.

topics.title: China-Linked Hackers Root Firewalls With PHP2Shell
topics.latest_developments: The Hacker News reported that the suspected China-nexus attacker rooted 25 servers in the operation researchers observed on October 25, 2026, drove AI through the post-exploitation work, and breached a United States government-affiliated network; SecurityWeek named the second exploit Fragnesia, a kernel privilege escalation the attacker fired after PHP2Shell to take root on firewalls and two of the organization's servers; and InfraTrust warned that PHP2Shell exposes the web management interfaces of firewalls, virtual private network gateways, and application delivery controllers.
topics.summary: PHP2Shell covers two remote code execution flaws the PHP Foundation patched out of cycle on October 21, 2026 in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35, and CISA has ordered federal agencies to fix both by October 29, 2026. Patch PHP everywhere it runs, including network appliances that embed it, and hunt for web shells on internet-facing servers.

sources.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit PHP2Shell to Root Firewalls

topics.title: Volt Typhoon's Silent Train Masks Zero-Days
topics.latest_developments: Lumen Technologies Black Lotus Labs attributed Silent Train to Volt Typhoon and said the covert access network, first identified in late 2023, rotated chains of compromised small office, internet-of-things, and enterprise devices through four separate zero-day exploitation campaigns before investigators disrupted it; Kim Zetter and BleepingComputer detailed the framework on October 28, 2026 as the first concrete account of the tradecraft United States officials have called sophisticated for years.
topics.summary: Volt Typhoon is the Chinese state-sponsored group that United States agencies accuse of pre-positioning inside power, water, and communications networks. Silent Train hides the origin of its intrusions behind freshly hijacked intermediate hosts, so defenders should hunt for inbound sessions relayed through small office routers and other edge devices instead of relying on known command-and-control addresses.

sources.title: Silent Train: Volt Typhoon's Sophisticated Infection Chain into US Targets Exposed
Volt Typhoon hides zero-day attacks using 'Silent Train' framework

topics.title: Firmware, Hypervisor, and Kernel Flaws Draw Attacks
topics.latest_developments: Wired and The Hacker News reported on October 28, 2026 that the critical firmware flaw sits in EDK II, the open-source code most hardware makers use to build UEFI firmware, dates back 16 years, and runs an attacker's code before Secure Boot only while a machine boots over the network, and CISA added two more actively exploited bugs to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog the same day: CVE-2026-41709, insufficient logging in Broadcom VMware ESX, and CVE-2026-46300, a missing variable initialization in the Linux kernel.
topics.summary: EDK II supplies the firmware that runs before any operating system on most servers in data centers worldwide, so the flaw gives an attacker on the network segment control of the machine from power-on. Turn off network booting where nobody needs it, chase firmware updates from server vendors, and patch VMware ESX and Linux hosts under Binding Operational Directive 26-04.

sources.title: Most Servers on the Planet Are Vulnerable to This Firmware Code-Execution Flaw
Critical 16-Year-Old UEFI Flaw Can Run Code Before Secure Boot on Network-Booting Servers

topics.title: GMO Tells Onamae Customers to Shut Down
topics.latest_developments: GMO Internet Group told Onamae.com Desktop Cloud customers to disconnect from the internet and power down their computers after the intruder who planted malware on as many as 26,739 customer servers threatened to encrypt systems on October 28, 2026, and the company refused the extortion demand and opened a reward program that day paying up to $1 million in total for tips that lead to an arrest or an international wanted notice; Japan Airlines added to the country's run of incidents, warning that hackers took passport numbers, frequent flyer numbers, email addresses, and phone numbers for about 2,000 customers.
topics.summary: Onamae.com Desktop Cloud hosts Windows desktops that Japanese customers use for foreign exchange trading. Customers should keep those machines offline until GMO clears them, and rotate every credential typed into the hosted desktops.

sources.title: Japan's GMO urges customers to shut down PCs amid ransomware threat

topics.title: Leak Exposes 41,000 Homeland Security Workers
topics.latest_developments: Wired reported on October 28, 2026 that leaked records cover 41,000 Department of Homeland Security workers, among them undercover Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents, and list the locations of ICE and Customs and Border Protection facilities, workers' cell phone numbers, and the membership of internal groups tied to wiretap programs, Palantir software, and xAI's Grok chatbot.
topics.summary: The records expose federal agents who work undercover and map the buildings they operate from, raising physical risk alongside the usual phishing and impersonation risk. Organizations that run informant-facing or covert programs should treat internal group membership lists as sensitive data and restrict who can export them.

sources.title: Massive Leak Exposes 41,000 Homeland Security Workers—Including Undercover ICE Agents

business_politics.title: Weil Gotshal Shuts Its Doors
business_politics.latest_developments: Weil Gotshal & Manges leaders told their partners Wednesday, October 28, that the firm should dissolve, and the firm confirmed it is shutting down, a day after it hired a bankruptcy lawyer and retained Davis Polk & Wardwell to weigh a merger, a slimmed-down successor, or a wind-down.
business_politics.summary: Weil, the New York firm that pioneered the modern corporate bankruptcy practice and ranked among America's largest and most prestigious partnerships for nearly a century, bled partners to higher-paying rivals and ran out of merger partners. The Wall Street Journal traces the collapse to competition that squeezed Weil's grip on the bankruptcy business it helped create, and The Economist reads the failure as a lesson in what superstar pay does to corporate loyalty.

business_politics.title: The Fed Decides Wednesday
business_politics.latest_developments: The Federal Reserve held rates steady Wednesday, October 28, despite elevated inflation, left the door open to an increase in December, and cut its 2027 calendar to seven policy votes from the customary eight; Wall Street read Chairman Kevin Warsh's news conference as reluctance to hike aggressively, stocks edged higher, Treasury yields split, Microsoft reported accelerating cloud growth on revenue up 19% to $92.3 billion, and Alphabet shares fell about 10% after a $51 billion quarterly capital outlay deepened its cash burn and its "AI mode" cut into traditional search.
business_politics.summary: The Fed's statement landed on the quarter's biggest earnings day, with hyperscaler results due the same afternoon. Big and regional banks alike report a surge in lending tied to artificial-intelligence buildouts, and their executives keep telling investors they remain cautious about it.

business_politics.title: Houthis Strike Ras Tanura and Oil Climbs
business_politics.latest_developments: Oil recovered most of two days of losses Wednesday, October 28, with crude topping $115 a barrel on fears that Washington renews strikes on Iran after the November 3 midterms, and the Wall Street Journal reported that Vice President JD Vance, acting at President Trump's direction, wrote to Iran's security chief to restart peace talks; United States natural gas futures gained 4.4% as the November contract expired.
business_politics.summary: Yemen's Houthi militants said Tuesday they hit Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's largest refinery, in the Eastern Province with a ballistic missile, a direct strike at the center of the kingdom's Gulf export complex. Washington has warned Gulf governments to expect a short, intense renewal of the fight with Tehran after the midterms, and Iran has told its citizens to curb consumption and its civil servants to work from home as natural gas runs short.

business_politics.title: Healey Delivers the Budget at 12:30
business_politics.latest_developments: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey's first Budget passed without a bond market wobble—gilts held their pre-Budget gains—as he raised taxes on banks and on income from savings and property to pay modest help with household energy bills; British lenders attacked the levy, the Office for Budget Responsibility called the outlook for living standards pretty grim, HM Revenue & Customs prepared a £1.3 billion squeeze that collects tax from the self-employed with each monthly payment, business leaders said the package fell short of the praise Healey gave them, and The Economist judged that he deferred Britain's deeper problems.
business_politics.summary: Healey had to cut energy bills without unsettling gilt investors who have punished every sign of fiscal slippage, after September inflation and 24.5 billion pounds of public borrowing both overshot forecasts. His fiscal rules require the government to cover day-to-day spending entirely from tax revenue and borrow only for investment by the fiscal year ending in April 2030, and the plans keep him inside them.

business.title: Pennsylvania Ranks Fourth in Data Centers
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Wednesday, October 28, that Pennsylvania now ranks fourth among the states in the number of data centers and that the state's new map of those facilities has critics.
business.summary: Pennsylvania's data center count puts the state behind only three others, and the power those buildings draw sits behind the electric rate increases Duquesne Light customers absorbed this month and the state study of restarting retired generating plants. Western Pennsylvania municipalities have fought over the facilities township by township, among them Upper Burrell in Westmoreland County, which adopted a data center zoning ordinance on October 22.

business.title: Mortgage Rates Stay Above 7%
business.latest_developments: WTAE reported Wednesday, October 28, that the Federal Reserve's decision to hold interest rates steady keeps mortgage rates above 7% and raises the monthly cost homebuyers carry, with the war against Iran feeding the inflation that stayed the Fed's hand.
business.summary: Rates above 7% bind the Pittsburgh housing market, where sellers have listed houses across the region and buyers have stayed home. Energy prices run through the arithmetic: crude topped $115 a barrel Wednesday, and the inflation that follows keeps the Fed from cutting.

business.latest_developments: Pittsburgh International Airport ran its annual winter readiness exercise along a runway Wednesday, October 28, putting the plow, broom, and deicing crews who call themselves the Snow Fighters through the routine they will run all winter.
business.summary: The airport's operations crews describe the work as a choreographed dance performed by multi-ton machines, and one of them told WTAE it amounts to a Super Bowl every year. The drill follows the January storm that buried Western Pennsylvania under more than a foot of snow in a matter of hours.

business.latest_developments: TribLive reported Wednesday, October 28, on Koreyinz, a food truck that bills itself as Pittsburgh's first modern boba tea maker and sets out to widen what the region drinks.
business.summary: Boba, the sweet tea-based drink with chewy tapioca pearls, has had a following in Pittsburgh for years, served in colorful cups through a thick straw. The couple behind Koreyinz run the truck on the premise that the local palate is ready for a newer generation of the drink.

business.title: Cestra Takes the West Penn Multi-List Presidency
business.latest_developments: Howard Hanna said Wednesday, October 28, that shareholders elected its executive Dennis Cestra Jr. president of West Penn Multi-List in a vote held last month.
business.summary: West Penn Multi-List operates the multiple listing service through which Western Pennsylvania real estate agents post and share homes for sale, which makes its presidency a seat at the center of the regional housing market. Cestra comes to the job from Howard Hanna, the region's largest brokerage.

business.title: KP Threads Takes a Greensburg Storefront
business.latest_developments: Kelly Pruss, a Greensburg native, has moved her three-year-old branded apparel business, KP Threads, into a storefront at the corner of South Urania and Euclid avenues in her hometown, TribLive reported Wednesday, October 28.
business.summary: Pruss spotted a for-rent sign in the window and took the space for the boutique, which sells branded apparel and had operated without a Greensburg shopfront. The move adds a retail tenant to a Westmoreland County downtown that has worked for years to fill vacant storefronts.

sources.title: Greensburg native moves branded apparel business KP Threads to hometown storefront

business.title: National Operators Dominate Pennsylvania Medical Marijuana
business.latest_developments: TribLive reported Wednesday, October 28, that multistate companies now control most of Pennsylvania's medical marijuana market, a decade after the state legalized it.
business.summary: Former state senator Daylin Leach, who pushed the legalization law through Harrisburg, told the paper he once knew the name of everyone running a dispensary in Pennsylvania. Consolidation matters as the legislature keeps debating adult-use legalization, which would hand the same national operators a far bigger market.

sources.title: National companies dominate Pa.'s medical marijuana market

business.title: Pittsburgh City Paper Turns 35
business.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper published a package Wednesday, October 28, marking 35 years since its 1991 founding, including an accounting of the back-page advertising that paid the bills.
business.summary: The alt-weekly's staff recount a newsroom that doubled as a journalistic proving ground, and one column puts the adult-services ads that ran in the back pages during the 1990s at $15,000 to $20,000 a week, revenue typical of alt-weeklies then. A companion history traces the Pittsburgh Courier and OUT Magazine as the paper's predecessors in the city's alternative press.

around_town.title: Five Things in the Zoning Package
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive laid out five takeaways Wednesday, October 28, from the zoning package Pittsburgh City Council passed Tuesday, October 27, after years of debate and heavy revision.
around_town.summary: The package carries the citywide inclusionary zoning requirement that council gave final approval Tuesday, the measure that obliges developers of larger residential projects to set aside affordable units. The arguments ran for years and the bill shrank along the way.

around_town.title: City Hall Claims Progress on Permits
around_town.latest_developments: Pittsburgh leaders pointed Wednesday, October 28, to early gains in the city's permit overhaul and promised further changes, with Councilman Anthony Coghill citing his own waits on city permits.
around_town.summary: Pittsburgh's permit office processes the approvals every builder, contractor, and homeowner needs before work starts, and delays there have drawn complaints from developers and council members alike. Coghill and the administration say more of the overhaul is coming.

sources.title: Pittsburgh leaders tout early progress in permit reform, vow more overhauls to come

around_town.title: Guy Challenges Deluzio in the 17th
around_town.latest_developments: KDKA reported Wednesday, October 28, that Republican Beaver County Sheriff Tony Guy faces an uphill race against Democratic Representative Chris Deluzio in Pennsylvania's 17th Congressional District, with analysts pointing to President Trump's sinking poll numbers as the reason.
around_town.summary: The 17th District covers Beaver County and part of Allegheny County, and Deluzio has held the seat since 2023. KDKA calls Guy's campaign a one-man show, and voters decide the race Tuesday, November 3.

around_town.title: Skill Game Money Lifts Garrity
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Wednesday, October 28, that skill game interests have driven Republican candidate Stacy Garrity's fundraising in the closing weeks of the Pennsylvania governor's race against Governor Josh Shapiro.
around_town.summary: Skill games are the slots-like machines that sit in bars, clubs, and convenience stores across Pennsylvania, and Harrisburg has fought for years over taxing and regulating them. The industry's money now flows into the November 3 contest that decides who signs or vetoes any such law.

sources.title: Skill games boost Garrity's fundraising in final weeks of Pa. governor's race

around_town.title: Trees Go Back In on the North Shore
around_town.latest_developments: WTAE reported Wednesday, October 28, that crews have begun replanting trees on Pittsburgh's North Shore near Acrisure Stadium.
around_town.summary: Nearly 100 trees and bushes came out of the ground around Acrisure Stadium to make room for the NFL draft stage Pittsburgh hosted this year. The replanting restores the landscaping along the riverfront walkway and plaza that fans cross on game days.

sources.title: Trees returning to Pittsburgh's North Shore near Acrisure Stadium

around_town.title: Money Floods Three Suburban House Races
around_town.latest_developments: PublicSource tallied campaign spending Wednesday, October 28, in three Pittsburgh-area state House races, finding Republican Representative Valerie Gaydos outspent by her challenger in the airport-area district west of Pittsburgh, a Democrat leading the money race in Cranberry, and the Republican incumbent holding the fundraising edge in southern Allegheny County.
around_town.summary: The three seats sit among the handful that could flip control of the Pennsylvania House on Tuesday, November 3, and the fundraising gaps show where each party sees an opening. Gaydos has held her Allegheny County district since 2018.

sources.title: Campaign spending takes off in airport-area Pa. House race

around_town.title: Federal Monitors Stay Outside Allegheny County Polls
around_town.latest_developments: County officials said Tuesday, October 27, that United States Department of Justice Election Day monitors will not enter any of Allegheny County's more than 1,300 polling places, and Westmoreland County expects no federal monitors at all, narrowing the deployment reported last week.
around_town.summary: Pennsylvania law limits who may stand inside a polling place, so the federal monitors assigned to Allegheny County will work from outside on Tuesday, November 3. The Post-Gazette published its guide to the election the same week, covering where and how to vote and the mail ballot rules.

around_town.latest_developments: TribLive reported Wednesday, October 28, that the three-year rehabilitation of the Tarentum Bridge has moved to 2028, a year later than planned.
around_town.summary: The bridge carries Route 366 over the Allegheny River between Tarentum and New Kensington, and the project will bring extended detours and traffic tangles to Alle-Kiski Valley commuters once it starts. The delay gives drivers an additional year before the closures begin.

around_teams.title: Graham's Disguised Zones Rate Among the Best
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette's film study, published Wednesday, October 28, rates the disguised zone coverages that Steelers defensive coordinator Patrick Graham calls among the best in the NFL.
around_teams.summary: Graham's unit shows a quarterback one picture before the snap and rotates into another after it, a scheme the Post-Gazette credits for the run-stuffing and late takeaways that carried the Steelers to 5-2 through the win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris. The Steelers host the Cleveland Browns on Sunday, November 1, at 1 p.m. on CBS.

around_teams.title: Dulac and SNR Drive Close the Books on Paris
around_teams.latest_developments: Gerry Dulac took reader questions in his Post-Gazette Steelers chat Wednesday, October 28, and the team's channel posted Tuesday's SNR Drive, on which Matt Williamson and Wes Uhler spent the first 20 minutes on the Paris trip itself before working through the Week 7 win over the New Orleans Saints and the rest of the league's weekend.
around_teams.summary: The Steelers return from France at 5-2 and host the Cleveland Browns on Sunday, November 1, at 1 p.m. on CBS. SNR Drive runs on the Steelers' own channel, and the hosts note that their opinions belong to them rather than the team.

around_teams.title: Hiles on the Kordell Stewart Documentary
around_teams.latest_developments: Post-Gazette columnist Noah Hiles wrote Wednesday, October 28, that HBO's new documentary on Kordell Stewart should make Steelers fans uncomfortable.
around_teams.summary: Stewart quarterbacked the Steelers from 1995 to 2002, took them to two AFC championship games, and absorbed years of abuse from the fan base and talk radio. Hiles argues the film puts that treatment back in front of the people who delivered it.

team_usa.title: Juventus Tracks Balogun
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN's Transfer Talk reported Wednesday, October 28, that Juventus has an interest in Folarin Balogun, the United States men's national team striker who plays for AS Monaco.
team_usa.summary: Balogun has filled the center-forward role for the United States and now plays in Ligue 1 with Monaco. A move to Turin would put him alongside his national teammate Weston McKennie, who scored for Juventus against Lecce on Sunday, October 25.

team_usa.title: Pulisic Nears a Milan Extension
team_usa.latest_developments: Sources told ESPN on Wednesday, October 28, that Christian Pulisic will sign a four-year AC Milan contract running through 2031.
team_usa.summary: Pulisic, the captain and leading attacker of the United States men's national team, has become Milan's central forward threat and scored in the club's 2-0 win over Udinese on Sunday, October 25. The deal would keep him in Serie A through the 2030 World Cup cycle.

team_usa.title: Eddie Johnson Takes In the Florida Three-Year-Old
team_usa.latest_developments: Former United States men's national team forward Eddie Johnson said Monday, October 26, that his academy will train the three-year-old boy whom a Florida youth soccer program removed last weekend after tensions over the child's play.
team_usa.summary: Johnson scored 19 goals in 63 appearances for the United States and now runs a youth academy. His offer followed a weekend in which police were called to the Florida youth program over the dispute.
